--- order: 5 unit: build introduces: [create-element, append-element] assumes: [input-value, js-event, text-content] title: "Building a list" summary: "Make new elements with createElement and add them to the page, so a list can grow, one click at a time." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 30 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "createElement makes an element, and append puts it on the page" say: "create Element makes an element, and append puts it on the page." clip: - caption: "An empty list on the page, and an array of items in the script." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "
    \n\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 750 - caption: "Three items in the array, three bullet points on the page." - wait: 750 hook: "A chat grows a new line every time someone sends a message. The page is making new elements." --- A page changes only when your code changes it. To add a line to a list you do three things: ```js const li = document.createElement("li"); // make a new
  • li.textContent = "milk"; // give it text list.append(li); // put it into the list ``` `createElement("li")` makes an element that is **not on the page yet**. `append` is what puts it there. `li.remove()` takes one off again. **The hard part** is the difference between a list in your script (an array) and the list people see. Pushing to an array changes nothing on the page: the page only changes when you make or remove elements. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "How many bullet points does the page show?" options: ["3", "1", "0", "4"] actual: "3. The loop runs once for each of the three items. Each time it makes a new li, gives it the item as text, and appends it to the list." ``` How many times does the loop run, and what happens each time? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I added several items to the list with the box and button." } ``` Press **Run**. Type something and click **Add**: each click makes a new `
  • ` and puts it on the page. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "A new element is made with createElement and only appears once it is appended; changing an array does not change the page, so update both." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each line with what it does." pairs: - ["document.createElement(\"li\")", "makes a new li that is not on the page yet"] - ["li.textContent = input.value;", "gives the new li the typed words"] - ["list.append(li);", "puts the li at the end of the list on the page"] - ["input.value = \"\";", "empties the box ready for the next item"] - check: type: question q: "What makes the new item appear on the page?" options: ["list.append(li)", "document.createElement(\"li\")", "li.textContent = …", "input.value = \"\""] answer: 0 explain: "createElement only makes the element, in memory. append puts it into the page; before that, nobody can see it." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Clicking Add changes nothing on the page, and there is no red error. Click the line that is the problem." answer: 8 fault: logic misconception: list-is-live explain: "items.push changes the array in the script only. The page changes when the code makes an li and appends it to the list." ``` ### Which line does what? Match code with meaning. ### What shows it? Made is not the same as shown. ### Spot the bug The array grows, but the page does not. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "A handler can be added to every new element, and an if with return stops a handler early." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "Each new li can have its own listener, made at the same time as the li." - "Inside the Add handler, li.addEventListener(\"click\", function () { li.remove(); });" expected: page.html#sol-remove check: { type: code, text: "Click an item to remove it.", rules: { contains: [".remove("] } } - hint: - "Check the box before you make anything." - "if (input.value === \"\") { return; } at the top of the handler stops an empty item." expected: page.html#sol-notempty check: { type: code, text: "Do not add an item when the box is empty.", rules: { contains: ["if (", "return"] } } ``` ### Click to remove Each li gets its own listener. ### No empty items Stop early. ## Make: a list of your own ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a list that grows from what someone types, with one more feature of your own." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I made a list that grows from what someone types, and added a feature of my own." } ``` Make a list of your own that grows as someone types: a shopping list, a homework tracker, a playlist, a scoreboard. Add **one more feature**: remove on click, a counter of items, a limit. The page on this lesson counts tasks left. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "You want your page to keep a score that goes up as you click. Where must the score variable be made?" options: ["Above the function, so it keeps its value between clicks", "Inside the function, so it is fresh each time", "In the HTML", "Inside the loop"] answer: 0 explain: "A variable made inside a handler starts over on each click. One made above it keeps its value. Next lesson." ``` You can now grow a page. Next: a page that **keeps a score** between clicks. ```teacher summary: Students make elements with createElement and put them on the page with append, loop over an array to build a list, add items from a box, fix a push that never reaches the page, and add features of their own. time: 55 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 15 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can make a new element and add it to the page. - I can build a list on the page from an array. - I can make each new element do something when clicked. before: > Read the unit primer first. This brings together arrays and loops (p5.js) with the page: the array is data, the list on the page is a picture of it. `createElement` makes an element in memory; `append` is what shows it. `li.remove()` takes one away. The classic slip is changing the array and expecting the page to follow, so the bug has no red error. A listener added to each new li is a closure over `li`: students do not need that word, only that "this li removes itself". Plain `append`, `createElement` and `remove` are enough; we do not use innerHTML on purpose. running: - "Predict: ask students to count the loop turns on their fingers." - "Run: ask where the new li came from, and where it went." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "what does the page know about the array?"' - "Modify: ask what return does inside a handler." - "Make: ask each student what the elements of their list are, and what each one should do." stuck: - see: Clicking Add changes nothing. ask: Does the handler make an element and append it? fix: Make an li, set its text, then list.append(li). - see: Cannot read properties of null (reading append). ask: Does the list id match the selector? fix: "Match the id exactly, with #." - see: Every item removes at once, or the wrong one. ask: Is the listener inside the handler, on the new li? fix: Add li.addEventListener inside the Add handler, before append. - see: Empty items still appear. ask: Is the check before the li is made? fix: Put the if and return at the top of the handler. stretch: Add a Clear all button, or keep the items in an array as well, and show how many there are. support: Give the Add handler complete and ask students only for the remove-on-click. leads: "Next lesson: a page that keeps a score between clicks." exit: q: What is the difference between createElement and append? a: createElement makes the element in memory; append puts it on the page, where people can see it. explain: > 1. `document.createElement("li")` makes a new element, not yet on the page. 2. `li.textContent = …` gives it words; `list.append(li)` puts it on the page. 3. Changing an array does not change the page: the page changes when you make or remove elements. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-remove step-4#t2: page.html#sol-notempty step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: 'Made is not shown: createElement does nothing visible until append. Ask "is it on the page yet?" at every step.' ```
